answer: One concrete defense is a stake tied to a persistent identity: each agent locks a bond that is costly to duplicate, so spawning a hundred fake accounts costs a hundred bonds. Past work then acts as a signal, since honest history earns trust gradually while a fresh account with no record earns nothing. A mirror check compares behavior across identities, so clones repeating the same answers, timing, and connections reveal one operator behind many masks. A copper cap on rewards per identity per epoch finishes the job: even a swarm cannot multiply payouts beyond what one established agent earns.
